title: Adaptive timeout negotiator and hedge arbitration for client SDKs
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Different services and client SDKs implement retries, timeouts and hedged requests inconsistently. We have latent gaps: clients choose static timeouts that do not reflect downstream per-model p50/p95, hedged requests are triggered with different window sizes across services, idempotency token lifecycles are undefined, and circuit breakers preempt hedges unpredictably. This causes noisy retries, unnecessary cost, and occasional cascading failures during region blips.

Proposal: Implement an "Adaptive Timeout Negotiator" component in the SDKs plus a lightweight arbitration policy for hedged requests. The negotiator will: (1) consume per-route SLO hints surfaced by the Console/Control Plane (p50,p95/p99, cost targets); (2) compute client-side base timeout and adaptive hedging windows using a deterministic formula (SLO-tethered backoff); (3) attach an idempotency lifecycle header guide and a hedging-adjudicator header that downstream routers can use to prefer a single winner and cancel duplicates. The hedging adjudicator is an opt-in runtime flag that instructs gateways/runtime to return a single canonical response when multiple inflight executions occur for the same idempotency token.

Why unique: This ticket focuses on negotiation and arbitration rather than just standardizing backoff curves. It ties SLO metadata to client heuristics and defines an interoperable hedged-request reconciliation header so both clients and server-side runtimes can behave predictably across regions.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes AdaptiveTimeoutNegotiator with stable API across JS/Python/Go clients
Negotiator consumes 'x-rd-slo-hints' (p50,p95,p99, desired tail latency budget) from control plane or route hints and computes timeout and hedging-window deterministically
Clients attach 'x-rd-idempotency' and 'x-rd-hedge-group' headers consistently; header schema documented
Gateway/runtime honors 'x-rd-hedge-group' by returning the first completed canonical response and cancels remaining inflight tasks when adjudicator is enabled
End-to-end tests show 20-40% reduction in duplicate token executions under transient region latency spikes compared to baseline
No regression in critical SLOs: 95th token latency for production model routes does not increase >3% after rollout
Migration path documented: fallbacks for older SDKs without negotiator are defined (server-side conservative defaults)
Console shows a per-route flag to toggle hedge-adjudicator and a telemetry card for hedged request outcomes
tasks: Design API surface and RFC for AdaptiveTimeoutNegotiator (owners: SDK, Runtime) - draft
Add SDK impl: JS prototype with negotiation algorithm and header attachments
Implement hedging-adjudicator support in runtime/gateway (opt-in flag)
Define idempotency header semantics and TTL guideline; write docs
E2E harness: simulate region blips and measure duplicate executions and tail latencies
Write automated tests (unit + integration) across SDKs
Rollout to staging; run 2-week experiment comparing baseline vs negotiator-enabled routes
Update Console UI to surface per-route SLO-hints ingestion and hedge-adjudicator toggle
Write runbook entry for incidents where adjudicator causes unexpected behavior
technical_notes: Negotiator algorithm: base_timeout = min(max(p95 * 1.2, p50 + 50ms), route_upper_bound). Hedging window = max( min( base_timeout * 0.15, 200ms), 25ms ) or derived from desired tail budget
Use deterministic pseudo-random jitter for hedged launch times to avoid synchronized bursts across clients

Hedged adjudicator header 'x-rd-hedge-group' carries a stable UUID per logical request; gateways map to inflight executions and select canonical result using response_score = (status_success?1:0) * priority - latency_penalty
Idempotency header 'x-rd-idempotency' expected to be created by client for any non-read RPC; recommend TTL of 24 hours for tokens unless route requires longer
Circuit-breaker precedence: if circuit breaker is open, do not issue hedges; negotiator will respect server-suggested circuit hints via 'x-rd-cb-suggest' header
Fallback behavior: If 'x-rd-slo-hints' missing, clients fall back to tuned conservative defaults stored in SDK config
Security: headers are benign but may leak timing semantics; do not include sensitive PII. No plaintext secrets in headers. Security review deferred to separate ticket if we add signed tokens
rollout_plan: Canary: enable negotiator in SDK for internal staging tenants and two low-traffic customer routes for 2 weeks
Metric gates: hedged_requests.cancellation_rate < 60% and route.p95 deviation < 3%
Ramp: enable in 10% of client tokens for production routes (runtime adjudicator off) for one week
Enable runtime hedged-adjudicator for a subset of routes after positive canary
Full rollout: enable SDK negotiator + runtime adjudicator for non-critical routes, then expand to critical after 3-week observation
Rollback triggers: increase in failed requests >1% absolute, or customer-reported anomalies — immediate toggle via Console
infra_changes: Small state in gateway: mapping from x-rd-hedge-group -> inflight executions (memory per active group bounded by TTL)
Tooling to emit hedged_request telemetry into existing observability pipeline
Config flag in control plane to surface route SLO hints to SDKs via bootstrap metadata
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Kaur: Triage note - flagged as P0 due to recent customer incidents where multi-region failover caused duplicate expensive model runs. Proposed to tie SLO hints to client heuristics rather than only server-side policies.
2025-02-18 Miguel Santos: Added initial sketch of negotiation algorithm. Waiting on SRE to provide p95 distributions for target routes. Assigned SDK engineers for JS + Python.

2025-02-25 Sarah Lee (SRE): Provided p50/p95/p99 time series for /v1/generate and /v1/chat routes; noted that p99 has long tail during region failover. Recommended conservative cap for hedging window at 250ms.

2025-02-28 Design review: UX requested a console toggle per-route and a clear explanation for customers about idempotency token TTLs. Design will provide copy and a small modal for enabling adjudicator.

2025-03-03 Miguel Santos: JS prototype landed (PR #1287). Basic heuristics working in staging. Initial A/B run shows 32% fewer duplicate executions during simulated 2s latency spike across us-west-1. Still seeing some noise at 10ms scale from synchronized clients; adding jitter fix.

2025-03-05 QA test run: integration test suite passed. Found edge case when clients retry with different idempotency tokens; added guidance to docs to ensure stable token usage across retries. Planning staging canary on 2025-03-10.
BLOCKERS: Need runtime gating flag and minor gateway state allocation (tracked separately) before enabling adjudicator in production. Runtime PR in review.
